title: Hosted canary rollout workflow — GA initiative tracker (Console + routing + policy + telemetry)
creator: Marissa Cole
description:
Summary
We are taking existing rollout primitives (model versioning, fallback routing, observability) and shipping a GA “Hosted canary rollout workflow” for percentage-based traffic splitting on Hosted routes. This is a cross-surface launch across Console (workflow + UI), Platform Control Plane (policy evaluation + config persistence), Smart Routing/Data Plane (traffic splitting enforcement), and Telemetry/SRE (stop conditions, metrics, reliability).

Customer problem
Customers want to introduce a new model version/config safely without downtime or blind risk. They need:
- Gradual rollout schedule (1% → 5% → 25% → 50% → 100%)
- Clear visibility into baseline vs canary metrics
- Guardrails (max step size, soak times, approvals)
- Auditable change history (who changed what, when)
- Fast rollback with predictable behavior

GA scope (Hosted)
1) Console workflow (GA)
- Wizard: select Hosted route, choose baseline + canary target (model version/config), define schedule + guardrails, review + confirm.
- Execution UI: show current step, next action, soak timers, approvals needed, and rollback controls.
- Rollout timeline / activity panel visible to customers (human-readable + linked to audit events).

2) Traffic splitting enforcement (GA)
- Deterministic cohorting for baseline vs canary.
- Cohorting consistent for retries and across streaming requests.
- Region-aware enforcement that matches existing Hosted routing behavior.

3) Policy guardrails + approvals (GA)
- Defaults + policy evaluation for:
  - max step size / max % jump
  - minimum soak time per step
  - approval gates (role-based) for start + step increases + rollback
  - entitlements and admin controls (who can create vs who can approve)
- Console shows policy failures as actionable errors (not generic “forbidden”).

4) Telemetry + stop conditions (GA)
- Baseline vs canary cohort metrics for Hosted routes (latency p50/p95, error rate, timeouts; plus throughput/tokens where available).
- Automatic stop/pause/rollback on SLO breach (initially focused on infra metrics; quality metrics optional/manual input for GA).
- Dashboards + alert templates for internal monitoring, plus customer-facing comparison view in Console.

5) Auditability (GA)
- Audit log events for rollout create/start/step-change/pause/approve/rollback/auto-stop.
- Customer-visible activity timeline that corresponds to audit events (with actor identity where permitted).

Non-goals for GA
- Multi-armed bandits / dynamic optimization.
- Automated quality gating as a hard block (support as optional signals/manual decision; expand post-GA).
- Dedicated/Private GA parity (maintain schema compatibility and avoid dead-ends, but Hosted is GA target).

Milestones
- Requirements locked + cross-team sign-off (PM + Eng + SRE + Sec): target 2025-02-14
- Design spec ready for build (wizard + timeline + comparison): target 2025-02-21
- Beta (design partners) enablement starts (feature-flagged): target 2025-03-07
- Beta exit / GA readiness review: target 2025-03-28
- GA ship + staged enablement: target week of 2025-04-01

Launch plan (high level)
- Beta: per-tenant enablement behind kill switch; limit to a small set of routes per partner; SRE monitoring required.
- Staged GA: dogfood → 10% tenants (opt-in) → broader availability; keep ability to disable UI + enforcement independently if needed.

Success metrics
- Product: % of eligible Hosted customers using canary rollouts within 60 days; reduction in “manual cutover” support tickets.
- Reliability: no increase in incident rate attributable to rollout enforcement; stop conditions prevent prolonged degradation.
- Usability: customers can execute a rollout end-to-end without support in < 10 minutes for common cases.

Open questions (needs resolution before GA go/no-go)
1) Default stop thresholds by tier/region
- Are defaults global or tiered (e.g., enterprise vs self-serve)?
- Which signals are hard stop vs warn-only?
Owner: Sean Gallagher + Paula Mendes

2) Approval semantics for auto-rollback
- If auto-rollback triggers, do we require an approval to resume forward progress?
- Do we allow “auto-pause” vs “auto-rollback” per tenant policy?
Owner: Jordan Lee + Marcus Lin

3) Deterministic cohort key
- Confirm hash inputs for stickiness (request_id vs user_id vs API key) and behavior for missing keys.
- Ensure streaming/retry behavior doesn’t double-count or flip cohorts.
Owner: Mina Haddad + Ravi Menon

4) Audit log retention + customer export messaging
- Confirm retention defaults for Hosted audit events, and what is promised in docs vs enterprise packaging.
Owner: Kevin Osei + Elliot Price

5) Cardinality limits for cohort metrics
- Confirm which dimensions are exposed in customer UI vs internal only.
- Ensure no explosion by rollout_id + route + region.
Owner: Logan Wright + Thomas Baird

Notes / coordination
- This ticket is the top-level GA tracker. Please keep cross-team updates here weekly (or on milestone change), and log any scope changes explicitly with rationale.
- For GA scope changes, link the Slack decision thread and update the PRD “Out of scope” section to match.
acceptance_criteria:
GA exit criteria (must-have)
- Console workflow:
  - Create rollout on Hosted route with baseline + canary target
  - Start rollout and progress steps (manual)
  - Pause/resume and rollback available at all times (subject to policy)
  - Clear status + next action shown; errors actionable
- Enforcement:
  - Traffic split enforced at data plane per rollout config
  - Deterministic cohorting validated in staging and at least 2 beta tenants
  - Region behavior documented and matches enforcement
- Policy/guardrails:
  - Max step size + min soak time enforced
  - Approval gates enforced with RBAC role(s) and clear UI messaging
- Telemetry:
  - Baseline vs canary cohort metrics visible in Console (latency p50/p95, error rate, timeouts)
  - Stop conditions wired to orchestrator to pause/rollback
  - Internal dashboards available for on-call triage
- Auditability:
  - Audit log events emitted for rollout actions (including auto-stop/rollback)
  - Customer-visible timeline matches actions taken
- Operational readiness:
  - On-call runbook published; support escalation path documented
  - Feature flags + kill switch tested; backout plan documented
- Documentation:
  - Hosted canary rollouts docs published (Console walkthrough + APIs + troubleshooting)
  - Release notes drafted and reviewed

Beta exit signals (recommended)
- At least 3 design partners complete a full rollout to 100% and at least 1 rollback scenario.
- No P0/P1 unresolved issues in enforcement, policy, or metrics correctness.
comments: 2025-02-03 (Marissa Cole): Kickoff completed with Console/Control Plane/Routing/SRE/Sec. Agreed GA is Hosted-only; Dedicated/Private schema compatibility is a requirement but not a ship blocker.

2025-02-10 (Paula Mendes): Added initial stop-condition proposal to PRD. SRE request: ship with conservative defaults + per-tenant override capability, and ensure alerts don’t page on every step change.
2025-02-14 (Dylan Brooks): Console wizard flow locked pending final copy pass (warning states + destructive confirmations). Design iteration tracked in DES-742 and DES-755.

2025-02-21 (Jordan Lee): Policy precedence questions need ADR; current proposal: rollout policy checks evaluated before routing fallback policy application for user-initiated actions; enforcement in data plane remains best-effort but observable. Tracking in ADR (policy evaluation order).

2025-03-07 (Marissa Cole): Beta enablement started for first design partners under feature flag. Reminder: use per-tenant kill switch; do not enable without cohort dashboards + auto-stop wiring in place.

2025-03-12 (Sean Gallagher): SRE request after early beta: auto-stop should default to pause (not rollback) for latency regression until thresholds are tuned; rollback reserved for high-confidence signals (e.g., sustained 5xx/timeouts).

2025-03-18 (Marissa Cole): Scope trim confirmed: automated quality gating stays optional/manual for GA. We’ll provide UI affordance to attach a “quality note” to a step (timeline) but not block progression. Follow-up to be filed post-GA.
2025-03-22 (Marissa Cole): GA readiness review scheduled for 2025-03-28 with Eng/SRE/Sec. Please ensure ENG-9164 (E2E) and ENG-9171 (audit events) are green or have explicit mitigations.
